trait.name: Potions
entries: Dryleaf carries 2 flasks of {@item alchemist's fire|PHB}, and a {@item potion of healing|PHB}.

trait.name: Sneak Attack
entries: Dryleaf can inflict {@damage 3d6} damage with sneak attacks, as a 5th level rogue would.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Keen Smell
entries: As a cat, Farlane has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on smell.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Farlane is a 5th level spellcaster. Her spellcaster ability is Intelligence (spell save {@dc 14}, {@hit 6} to hit with spell attacks). She has the following spells prepared:

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 0} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}1 slashing damage.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the haunted pumpkin remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a regular pumpkin.

action.name: Choking Vines
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) piercing damage, and a Medium or smaller creature is {@condition grappled} (escape {@dc 12}). Until this grapple ends, the target is {@condition restrained}, and the pumpkin cannot use its vines on another target.

action.name: Vine Whip
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 10 ft., two separate targets. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) slashing damage.

action.name: Vine Whip
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 10 ft., two separate targets. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) slashing damage.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) slashing damage.

action.name: Choking Vines
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) piercing damage, and a Medium or smaller creature is {@condition grappled} (escape {@dc 14}). Until this grapple ends, the target is {@condition restrained}, as well as the creature.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) slashing damage.

trait.name: Amulet of Terror
entries: The amulet hanging from the King's neck allows him to manifest properly into this realm. It can be attacked at a disadvantage, but if done, the King receives damage as if he was vulnerable to the source.

action.name: Vine Hook
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage and the creature is pulled 15 ft towards the King. Until the King uses Vine Hook on a different creature or the affected creature succeeds on a {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) roll, they are {@condition grappled}.

action.name: Greatsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) slashing damage.

action.name: Illusionary Impalement {@recharge 5}
entries: The King gives a creature within 5 ft the illusion of being impaled in a horrifically painful manner by his sword. On a failed {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw, the creature suffers 17 ({@damage 4d6 + 3}) psychic damage, and it is {@condition frightened} until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, they suffer half the damage.

action.name: Vine Whip
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 30 ft., two separate targets. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) slashing damage.

action.name: Seed Blast {@recharge 6}
entries: The King of Pumpkins showers his enemies with burning seeds in a 20 ft-cone. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or suffer 21 ({@damage 6d6}) fire damage. On a successful save, suffer half as much.

reaction.name: Pumpkin Visage
entries: Once per round, when a creature within 30 ft declares an attack against the king, he may force them to succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} until the beginning of their next turn (interrupting the triggering attack).

item.name: Shattered Amulet Of Terror
entries: The amulet resembles a black bat, made of iron, holding a deep-blue cracked gemstone, resembling an eye.
While being attuned, the wearer can produce minor illusions and effects at will, much like the {@spell prestidigitation} cantrip. These must always be related to fear.
In addition, the wearer has advantage on Wisdom saving throws to avoid effects that would make them become {@condition frightened}, either magical or natural.
The caster can use these effects to give himself an advantage on a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. After this, the amulet loses its magic until the next midnight.

item.name: Scroll of Speak with Animals (Modified)
entries: This spell scroll can be used to cast {@spell speak with animals}. Its modification allows all party members that hear the spell to communicate with beasts for the duration.

contents.name: Rise of the Pumpkin King
headers: In This Town We Call Home

data.name: Rise of the Pumpkin King
entries: by Daniel Vilar
A festive adventure for 3rd to 4th level characters

entries.name: Summary
entries: While traveling along the road, the party finds the wreck of a recent raid, the wounded being dragged into nearby woods by the raiders: a troupe of pumpkins looking for a fight. Goldgrain's farmers hide in their homes and bar the windows, the curse of a witch burned at the pyre seems to fuel the anger of the vegetables, and an anxious alchemist works tirelessly on a solution potent enough to deal with the strange menace.

Fortunately, heroes have arrived to fend off the man-eating crops. What's causing the pumpkins to become alive and angry? Is it the curse of a long dead witch? Or is it something even more sinister? Why are they dragging the corpses of their victims away, and to where? Who commands them?
Soon enough, they'll find out answers to those questions, or perish under the wrath of the haunted crops.

entries.name: Using This Adventure
entries: The adventure is divided on segments based on location and tone. Any information on roleplaying the characters involved and on stat blocks are highlighted for ease of reference.

Encounters are balanced to be moderately dangerous towards a party of four with an average level of four. Encounters should be tailored to the party, if they're weaker or stronger due to numbers, level, or any other reason.

This adventure's specifications should be taken purely as guidelines, and players shouldn't be forced to stick to the plot if they're going in another direction. Rather, the adventure should be allowed to progress naturally.

entries.name: Getting Your Players Hooked
entries: The adventure starts on a road with woods nearby. There's various options on how the party finds themselves on the road. One might be a letter calling for help.
They may have heard rumors of merchant wagons disappearing on the road, or eavesdrop a conversation about a town haunted by the ghost of a witch.
If you want to give the party a potential sponsor, consider having a wealthy merchant named Walter request that they help him find his son, lost in the road.

entries.name: Pumpkins To Go

entries: From the road, you're able to see a wagon, stationed by the side of the road, yet you can't see a driver. As you get closer, the sound of something heavy being dragged over the ground reaches your ears, from behind the cart.

Behind its silhouette figures come forth. Overgrown pumpkins, vines thick as limbs and animated, but otherwise seemingly natural, are dragging the bodies of two guards and a merchant, towards the woods.
You can't but find it unsettling, how they seem to be staring at them without a face.

The {@b six {@creature Haunted Pumpkin|DVRotPK|pumpkins}} will not immediately spot the players, but will turn their attention towards them if they get reasonably close, attack them, or are noisy enough.

There's not a horse present, dead or alive. A {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, against passive perception if someone inspects the wagon, will reveal that the horse broke free of its reins and fled during the fight.

In combat, the {@creature Haunted Pumpkin|DVRotPK|pumpkins} try to surround the party, and restrain them using their {@i Choking Vines}, then keep choking them. They might use their {@i Vine Whip} to finish off weakened targets, or when they're not able to restrain anyone. They have no instinct of self-preservation, and will fight until they've been beaten to a pulp. Literally.

entries.name: I Was Just Pretending

entries: The last of the pumpkins crumbles in a pulp of sweet juices and seeds, with nary a sound. Immediately, you hear a crude sound, coming from the ground. It sounds like something in between a pained cough and a relieved sigh.

As you look down, you see the merchant you thought dead standing on his feet, not without effort. His clothes are torn from the pumpkins' thorny vines, and his pants suspiciously wet. Oddly enough, he seems rather gleeful.
"You're...really great! We didn't quite stand a chance there, much to my shame."
The young man turns towards you, and shakes the dirt off his clothes, still trembling. He looks at the vegetables, and offers a tired, nervous smirk.
"...They totally fell for it, too. I'm...quite the actor, am I not?"

The young man introduces himself as Wilburg, and thanks the party for saving him in a very physical, near uncomfortable manner. He then proceeds to narrate the raid, while using excessive body language and onomatopoeia, thanking the party once again. He anxiously avoids looking at the dead guards.
When he's done narrating and his adrenaline is done subsiding, he heads towards his wagon, and searches it in hopes of its contents being undamaged.

Wilburg immediately realizes his horse has fled for his life, an action he judges most wise, if not exactly convenient to them, and turns to the party, promising a reward of {@b 100 gold pieces} if they help him carry all the fabric they're able to salvage from the wagon to Goldgrain.

The party might also think about looking for his horse, whom Wilburg has given up on finding. A {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check is enough to track the exhausted animal, in which case Wilburg will reward them with {@b 50 gp} more.

entries.name: In This Town We Call Home

entries: After about an hour of walking, you get to the town of Goldgrain. Fallen leaves color the empty streets with the colors of autumn: you see, from time to time, guards patrolling the town, but otherwise its streets are empty.
In addition, almost every house you see has had its door and windows boarded up.

Townies are hiding from the pumpkins, and if their doors are banged, they react with relief the moment they realize the party are adventurers and urge them to head to the Hunter's Horn, an inn by the entrance of the town: the proprietress is a retired adventurer, and they are confident she can give them pointers in how to help them, and specially, offer a reward. When they get there, they will find the door isn't boarded up.

Although the inn notably lacks customers, the fireplace is lit. It fills the building with pleasant warmth, and prompts the monstrous skulls mounted on the walls, trophies gained in a life of adventure, to cut elongated, eerie shadows.
Behind the counter, an elderly woman pulls a crossbow down, with an apologetic look.
"My mistake. I haven't had customers in a while, and I feared you might be more of those pumpkins. Speaking of, may I offer you a slice of non-haunted pumpkin pie?"
After the apology, the proprietress, Joyce, explains the situation to the party:

items: Two weeks ago, hunters started disappearing around the outskirts of the forest nearby. Since they stopped leaving the town, pumpkins started attacking every few days.
Pumpkins want to drag their victims into the forest, killing them beforehand just to save themselves trouble. This makes Wilburg feel a little less smug about playing dead earlier, if present.

Joyce herself can offer little to no payment. If he was rescued, this prompts Wilburg to step in, and offer {@b 400 pieces of gold} as a reward for dealing with the crops, since he's stuck in the town until they are no more.

A year ago a witch that lived in the forest was burned at the stake following the kidnapping of several villagers, as well as turning Joyce's youngest son into a wolf. Townies convinced the pumpkins are the witch's spirit's doing, although this is not the case. Joyce gives the party the location of the witch's old hut in the forest, and suggests starting there

Belry Dryleaf, the local alchemist, has been tirelessly working on a solution to the pumpkin problem. His efforts have been, thus far fruitless, but she'll ask the party to check on him in case he has something to report.

entries.name: Dryleaf's Workshop
entries: It is not assumed that the players will visit Dryleaf's workshop, and they should not be forced to. If they do, however, they will find it unguarded, with the door unlocked

When you step in, the noises of paper cracking and water boiling fill your ears. You spot a halfling, whom you presume is Dryleaf, working frantically on the multiple tables, over which there's ingredients, notes, and tools scattered around. Without turning to look at you, he squeaks out, voice trembling:
"I've told you time after time, Joyce. When something finally works, I'll tell you, but I need to focus and I can't if you're around! Now, can you please leave be?"

entries.name: Roleplaying Wilburg
entries: Wilburg is a human male that doesn't seem older than in his early twenties, if he is even that old, and mostly seems to be excited and optimistic, very rarely seeming sad or angry, as well as absent minded. Extremely naive-looking for a merchant, the boy comes off as good natured, if rather clingy.
Heir of a wealthy merchant, he seeks to mimic his father's rise from humble origins to fortune, and will happily (and endlessly) talk about his father's achievements.
Wilburg has had a great and expensive education, being well versed in accounting, history, and geography. He is smart if rather gullible, and tends to state the obvious.
Although he admires his father greatly, he avoids relying on anything granted by him, as he wants to prove his own worth, and everything he can give to the party comes from his own pockets.

A success on a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal that, among the notes and scribbles scattered across the multiple tables of the room, there's a book which resembles a diary on its format. With a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check the party will be able to pick it up without {@creature Belry Dryleaf|DVRotPK|Dryleaf} becoming aware of it. The diary expresses the alchemist's feelings of guilt over the pumpkins, although it doesn't go into detail about why.

Once he becomes aware the party's identity, he'll be startled for a moment, and immediately ask to be left alone, patronizingly explaining he's really busy. This is only partially true: he's scared of the party being suspicious of him. A {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check tells he is nervous about their presence.
His eyes betray restless nights, and his twitchy behavior, fear. If asked for help to deal with the pumpkins, he's reluctant and alleges he can't afford resources.

In truth, he doesn't want the party to succeed. The magic words, a nice plea, and a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check... or the promise of a broken nose, and a {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check will be enough for him to give the party {@b 2 flasks of {@item alchemist's fire|PHB}} (PHB 148), and point at that the party "Should be smart to figure out plants hate fire".

If confronted with his diary, or enough suspicion as to believe he's in serious danger, he'll anxiously ask the party to hear him out. He tells the party the pumpkins are the result of him trying a formula that would make the crops grow much faster and bigger, and thus provide more resources and wealth for the town, but it was probably cursed by the witch's ghost.
He sobs on about his feelings of guilt and his incompetence as an alchemist, trying to gain sympathy from the party as well as paint himself in a good light.

A {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) will reveal that {@creature Belry Dryleaf|DVRotPK|Dryleaf} seems to be keeping something from the party. If they believe him, he'll hand them a {@item potion of healing|PHB}, in "good faith."

If the party does not believe him, he'll insist on his story being true, and should a fight break about, he will avoid actual confrontation, be it fleeing, calling for help, surrendering or, should he get really desperate, burn the workshop down.
One way or the other as long as conflict doesn't break out, he suggests looking at {@area the witch's hut|TheWitchsHut|x}, as the pumpkins seem to frequent that place.

entries.name: Roleplaying Joyce
entries: Joyce is an elderly human woman, on her late fifties. She's particularly kind towards adventurers, if she can come off as patronizing. Given the chance, she'll both give counsel and narrate her own adventures, specially at the Hunter's Horn.
A year ago, various villagers were kidnapped by the witch Julianna, her youngest son among them. The witch turned him into a wolf, and Joyce knows only as much about the rest.

entries.name: Roleplaying Dryleaf
entries: Belry Dryleaf is a male middle aged halfling. He seems to be perpetually anxious. Part of this is a natural tendency, but it's mostly due to guilt and fear for his life.
Dryleaf is the very definition of a coward. He will play victim, or say and offer anything if that ensures his survival, whether or not he can abide to his promises.

Years ago, Dryleaf worked with the witch Julianna in hopes of advancing his research. When rumors sparked, though, he snitched on the witch's activities, and grossly exaggerated them, leading to her execution.

While he feels a deep, genuine guilt over the fact, he's taken advantage of it, stealing the witch's scrolls and grimoires from her hut. This backfired terribly when he attempted to bind a fiend resting under a mound deep within the forest to do his bidding. This fiend, who calls himself the Pumpkin King, cursed the pumpkins to act as his minions, and blackmailed Dryleaf into cooperating.

He now works under fear for his life, as the fiend forces him to stuff the pumpkins inside corpses. He feels disgusted and guilty, but he's not brave enough to go against the entity's desires. He will under no circumstance admit this, unless caught at his lab deep within the mound.

entries.name: The Witch's Hut

entries: It doesn't take you much to reach a small clearing in the forest. On its edge, you see a small hut, covered in vines and uncared for. The forest is eerily silent and still, making the whole scene appear frozen in time.

When the party gets closer, a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will cause them to spot a black cat sitting over a branch, gazing over them. It remains at a safe distance from the party, and follows them inside, possibly startling them.

The inside of the hut it's composed of a single spacious room, that seems to be something in between a lab, kitchen, dining room and bedroom. The bed is the only part of the room that seems relatively undisturbed.

A layer of dust covers the whole interior, beneath which you spot the signs of a fight from long ago: broken vials in the ground, its contents long evaporated, burned patches on the floor, as well as crack and cuts on the wooden furniture.
There's a hatch under the bed, that the party will spot with a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, or without the need to roll if someone specifically looks under it.

Under the hatch, you find another room, this one smaller, without any means of ventilation. This makes the air feel stagnated and your breathing unpleasant. It appears to function as a small library, shelves cover the walls, filled partially with books and old scrolls, randomly arranged.

There are {@b two scrolls} the party finds if they search the library: A scroll of {@b {@spell burning hands} (Level 1)} and a scroll of {@b {@item Scroll of Speak with Animals (Modified)|DVRotPK|Speak with Animals (Modified)}}.

They can also find a journal covered in dust. Its cover has three waning crescent moons. The writings inside seem like readable gibberish. This is due to the journal being cyphered, and the three crescent moons represent the three steps back in the alphabet that one must take for each character in order to read it. Succeeding on a {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will crack the code. If someone figures out the moons are a hint, the roll is made at an advantage. Needless to say, if someone figures out how the code works, no roll is required.

Deciphering the journal will reveal that Julianna was making deals with a fiend trapped within a mound in the same forest, as well as point out the location of it. The fiend is described to be associated with fear and nightmares, but the writing seems intentionally vague. Anyone that reads the journal has advantage on {@skill Arcana} and {@skill Religion} checks involving this fiend.
There are also a few potions present, but a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check will reveal the potions have spoiled, and are not safe to drink
A character that drinks a spoiled potion needs to make a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw, or the pain in their stomach will render them {@condition poisoned} for 10 minutes.

If they find the scrolls, the black cat will directly interact with the party for the first time, and start meowing insistently at whoever holds the {@b {@item Scroll of Speak with Animals (Modified)|DVRotPK|Speak with Animals (Modified)}} scroll. Its modification allows all party members that hear the spell to communicate with beasts for the duration.

Should they cast it, the cat's meowing morphs into a soft and cultured yet insistent womanly voice. She appears to smile, before introducing herself as {@creature Farlane|DVRotPK|Farlane}, the old witch's familiar, and welcoming them to what's left of the hut.
Farlane then inquires for their reason of visiting her home. During the conversation:

items: She seems really bitter towards Goldgrain, not happy about her master being burned. Farlane might express even some satisfaction towards the pumpkins' raids.

If the witch's curse is mentioned, she'll chuckle, and playfully state there's no curse at all. She's telling the truth, and will explain that someone failed at binding an outsider to their bidding. Why that outsider is haunting pumpkins, she does not know.
If Dryleaf is mentioned at all, her hair and tail with rise up with a hiss. Regardless of who and how mentions him she tells the party what she thinks about him, and his story with her master.

She knows where the outsider has set his lair, and is more than willing to guide the players, if they accept making Dryleaf pay for his lies, whether that means exposing him to the town, which will probably end with him burning or locked away, or directly punishing him. Farlane is happy as long as she gets revenge for her mistress.
If the party asks her to decipher Julianna's journal, she'll playfully dodge the question. She will not outright refuse, but she just won't do it.

entries: After the conversation, if the party reached an agreement with Farlane, she tags along with them, telling them the location of the outsider's lair, a mound in the forest.
If they do not reach an agreement, she'll scoff, and leave the party to fend for themselves, sarcastically wishing them luck in their search.
One way or the other, when the party steps out of the hut, or if they are not able to find the hatch, they hear growling and the sounds of bushes shaking, as a pack of wolves scouts near the hut.

entries.name: Roleplaying Farlane
entries: Farlane is a black cat, and deceased witch Julianna's familiar. She's calm and observant, preferring to watch over events rather than participating in them.
She generally behaves in a chilly, sassy manner, she enjoys to toy with people more than having direct conversations, unless a topic particularly interests her.
She's fond of purring mid-phrase, and to respond to questions with a question of her own.
The cat is extremely bitter against Belry Dryleaf, due to him backstabbing her mistress and causing her execution, and will seek punishment against him given the chance.

entries.name: Wolves Hunt In Packs

entries: A deep, eager howl breaks the silence of the forest. From the woods, a pack of wolves emerges, the head of which looks huge and vicious. They are thin and malnourished, their jaws salivating in anticipation.

The pack is composed by {@b six {@creature wolf|MM|wolves}}, and led by {@b a single {@creature dire wolf|MM|direwolf}}. They are hostile towards the party, as the pack is starving. The pumpkins are driving prey away from their territory.
If the party casts {@spell Speak with Animals} or if they used the scroll earlier and the effect is still ongoing, the wolves only express their hunger for the time being.

The party may try to feed the wolves their rations, in which case, a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check is enough for the wolves not to attack while they try. If {@spell Speak with Animals} is active, and they communicate their intentions to the wolves, the check is made with advantage.

If a fight breaks, the wolves will focus on the front line, surrounding them, and taking advantage of their {@i Pack Tactics}. The wolves will fight until they're at half their HP, and then flee. The exception is the direwolf, who will not flee unless half the other wolves have already done so, and the odds are not looking in their favor. If the direwolf is incapacitated, the wolves will flee unless the odds seem clearly in their favor.

In the case the wolves are fed, they're grateful in the best manner they can express, possibly involving chorus barking. The only one that will think of outright thanking them verbally is the direwolf. This is due to being Joyce's youngest son, although he doesn't say so unless specifically asked. He doesn't remember much about that either, other than "The witch and the tiny man" making him that way.

entries.name: An Abomination Appears

entries: The creaking of trees being broken thunders in your ears. Another figure emerges from the woods, the carcass of a bear, its innards torn out, and instead, filled with several pumpkins. Roots cover the carcass, some going through it, and pull it like strings would a rather macabre puppet.

The {@creature Pumpkin Abomination|DVRotPK|pumpkin abomination} rushes towards the party, confident the fight with the wolves, that might have not occurred at all, has made the party easy targets. It relies on brute strength, and will prioritize the most dangerous looking members of the party, particularly if they wield fire. Like the pumpkins on the road, it has no regard for its self-preservation.
Once the party is done dispatching the beast, they can try to follow the trail back to the pumpkin's lair. A {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check is enough to succeed.

entries.name: Getting To The Lair
entries: By now, the party might have already discovered where the pumpkins are coming from, by either following the tracks, dealing with {@creature Farlane|DVRotPK|Farlane}, or finding {@area Julianna's journal|TheWitchsHut|x}. If they haven't by now, though, they could discover it by:

entries.name: Back in Goldgrain, have them find Dryleaf leaving his workshop.
entries: Make him look like he's worrying that someone is watching. This way, the party can tail him, and it can be satisfying if the group already suspected Dryleaf.

entries.name: Have one of the abductees come back to town.
entries: One of the victims dragged by the pumpkins manages to escape the lair, and comes to the town to tell the others about the horrors it has witnessed, men having their insides caved out, and dark cells inside a mound. They point out the location to the party, and beg them to rescue the others. This one is recommended if the party isn't suspicious about Dryleaf, so to keep it a twist.
Either way, the location of the lair is deep within the woods, in which the party finds the crumbling entrance to an old, deep mound within it.

entries.name: The Entrance

entries: You enter the mound, and immediately, its darkness surrounds you, prompting you to light a torch. There's an unpleasant humidity in the air, as well as the echoes of drops of water falling against the ground, mixed with the rustling of vines.
Just a few feet from the entrance, stairs go down in a spiral, for quite a while. Time has eroded the walls, leaving but silhouettes of engravings long faded.

After the stairs you come to a round cave-like area covered in vines. At the other side rests a slab of stone, covering the actual entrance the mound. It's guarded, too: You see two humanoid figures wearing rusty armor and gear, their barely visible flesh covered in vines. You can't help but suspect it is the same aberrant parasitism you saw in the bear's corpse.

The seal of stone is guarded by {@b 4 {@creature Haunted Pumpkin|DVRotPK|pumpkins}} and {@b 2 {@creature Pumpkin Puppet|DVRotPK|corpses}}. If the party looks under the armor of the corpses, there's a deep scar, under which rests a haunted pumpkin, without any innards inside the corpse.

The puppet-like corpses will try and restrain the closest members of the party. As they are not able to deal a lot of damage once they've grappled someone, they rely on the pumpkins to punish the party with their {@i Vine Whip}.
Once the party has dealt with the pumpkins, the seal can be pushed aside with a {@dc 16} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check, rolled with advantage if something is used as a lever.

On a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}), the party will spot a hole in the wall, close to the ground and wide enough for someone to attempt to crawl through it, although the tunnel is covered in tiny spikes, and anyone who tries to do so must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, in which they have advantage if their size is Small or less, or take 7 ({@damage 3d4}) piercing damage as they crawl over the spikes.

entries.name: Inside The Mound

entries: Once you're past the sealed archway, you see a wide, long corridor. It's entirely covered in thick, humid vines, specially the ground. On the walls, the vines almost entirely hide niches carved for the deceased, in which old bones rest, covered in mold.
At the end of the dark corridor, there's another set of stone stairs. The silence in the room is eerie, as you're only able to hear drops of water falling over the roots.

A {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) will reveal that, almost halfway across the corridor, there's a hole in the wall covered with vines, tall enough for someone to fit through while squatting. If {@creature Farlane|DVRotPK|Farlane} has tagged along with the party she'll point it out, most likely with {@spell Dancing Lights}, or by meowing nearby it.

A {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) will reveal that some of the thick vines covering the hall are faintly moving, A {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) will reveal three small pumpkins hiding among the vines that cover the ceiling.

Someone might consider it a good idea to light the vines on fire. In such a case, a {@dc 8} Intelligence saving throw will reveal that, given the very few means of ventilation, that would extremely dangerous. In any case, the humidity present on the corridor prevents non-magical fire from consuming the vines.

If someone tries to go across the hall, the vines will suddenly trap the character and try to strangle them. They receive 6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) damage per round, and a {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) is required to free oneself from them. The vines can also be destroyed, and have 10 HP. The pumpkins will try and wait to act as to catch as many members of the party simultaneously as they can. They will not be alerted on a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check.

Once the trap has been dealt with, the party can either proceed through the hole in the wall, if they spotted it, or down the stairs. If the former, they'll arrive to {@area Dryleaf's Lab|DryleafsLab|x}. Otherwise, if the party goes downstairs, they'll arrive to the lower level of the mound, {@area the throne of the Pumpkin King|TheKingAtHisThrone|x}.

entries.name: Dryleaf's Lab

entries: Behind the hole, you see a wide room full of tables, at the sides of it and at its center. Over the tables at the sides rest equipment and notes, and over the ones at the center, human-like shapes covered by blankets, as well as dry blood.
There's a sharp smell of iron in the air, mixed with sulfur and substances with a strong, nauseating basic odor that you're not able to recognize.
By the right side, there's a door that looks rather new, compared to the rest of the mound. Its small window secured by bars gives it a prison-like look.
But the one thing you notice the most, is the look of absolute terror that a halfling is giving you, a vial sliding from his hand, and shattering against the ground.

{@creature Belry Dryleaf|DVRotPK|Dryleaf} is found in the lab, absolutely terrified once he becomes aware of the party's presence. This goes double if {@creature Farlane|DVRotPK|Farlane} is accompanying the party. She'll start hissing at the halfling if that's the case

He will then surrender without putting up a fight, and any threat will be enough for him to crack and speak. If Farlane is present, he outright starts stuttering and begging for mercy. If given time to explain himself, tells the party the following story:

items: After the witch Julianna was executed, he retrieved a good amount of books and notes from her hut, and noticed quite a few mentioned a fiend bound to the mound, with whom the witch had a pact.
He tried to bind this fiend to his will for personal gain, but he failed, and instead released him.

The fiend calls himself the Pumpkin King, and raised the pumpkins to do his bidding. Dryleaf has thus been forced to empty corpses and place the pumpkins inside, so they have a body. He's not sure why he wants it that way, though. If he disobeys, the King has promised him eternal unrest.

entries: When he's done, he surrenders his fate to the party, who he dares not fight, and immediately offers to free the prisoners as a way of proving his feelings of guilt. If asked to do so, he will.

{@creature Belry Dryleaf|DVRotPK|Dryleaf} begs the party for mercy once he has surrendered, and promises to get away, never to return. If denied mercy, he gets more and more desperate. If he needs to, he offers the party indirect help against the Pumpkin King, though he will only give out {@b 2 flasks of {@item alchemist's fire|PHB}}. Anything else he promises the party he either cannot deliver, or will be an innocuous potion, which can be identified with a {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: If offered to leave
entries: Dryleaf will gladly accept, and tearfully thank the party. This will make Farlane visibly disappointed, and she will leave the party's company without a word. She's probably not able to pronounce any at the moment, either way.

entries.name: Should the party choose to restrain him instead
entries: Dryleaf doesn't put up a fight, only trying to escape when the party is not present. If Farlane is present, she's disappointed, but it's good enough for her, as long as he's given to Goldgrain's guard later.

No check is required to get resources out of him, but a compelling argument against his cowardice or exploiting his guilt, and a {@dc 19} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) will persuade him to participate against the Pumpkin King, if promised freedom afterwards. This will both annoy Farlane and make her curious, who will stick along the party if she was with them already.

entries.name: The King At His Throne

entries: You go down the stairs, and immediately see the wall on the left ceasing to be as it opens to a deep, wide circular dome-like room, its wall covered with niches and vines.
Over the ground rest old moldy bones and small pumpkins, both thankfully inert.

Opposite of where the stairs end, there's a throne made of thick, dry vines, the only dry ones on the mound. On it rests a figure dressed in black plated armor and proudly sporting a pumpkin head in which dark eyes and a mouth have been painted. By his side stand two corpses, just as you've encountered before. The figure then speaks in an echoing, deep voice.
"Welcome to my throne, although I don't recall inviting you. No matter. I am the Pumpkin King, and you will suffer your worst nightmares, never to awake."

entries.name: Roleplaying The Pumpkin King
entries: The fiend that calls himself the Pumpkin King is one of the least powerful ones among his kind, and he's painfully aware of it. This causes him to behave as he believes mortals think fiends are like, so he can induce terror. He's not a good actor, though, and it often comes off as overacted.
He harnesses power from the fear mortals have of him, and aims to terrify the people of Goldgrain, so he can then spread his horror to the whole realm.
This is the reason of him forcing Dryleaf to stuff pumpkins inside mortals: he hopes that the dark irony of it will fuel the nightmares of generations to come.

He will go on for a little gloating about his fiendish power, and generously offer the party to leave his lair, if they wish not to face eternal suffering. As he speaks, the roots shake and appear to burn, shadows seem darker, and pained moans can be heard beneath the ground. A {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) will reveal that these are merely harmless illusions. In addition, anyone that passes a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}) will note those manifestations do not correspond with any representation of a major fiend, and seem randomly put together.
If the party is unimpressed by the display, and refuses to leave, the fiend will be taken aback for a moment, and a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) reveals he's not confident about fighting.
The Pumpkin King denies any such claim, and after a moment, he reaffirms his might, and will lunge towards the party along his minions: {@b {@creature Pumpkin Puppet|DVRotPK|three pumpkin puppets}}.

During the fight, the King sports a greatsword, a black full-plate armor, and an amulet around his neck. He will let his minions take care of the front line, and focus on spellcasters, pulling them towards his reach with {@i Vine Hook}. He'll use {@i Illusionary Impalement} as often as he's able to, focusing on the characters that seem most dangerous to him.

The king's amulet looks like an iron bat holding a dark-green jewel shaped like an eye. It shines brightly whenever the king uses any magic. It can be stolen with a {@dc 21} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) and destroyed in a single action afterwards — though a failed attempt will get the king's attention.
When the King's HP reaches 0, the amulet will crack loudly. Any remaining minion dies instantly, and their pumpkin "corpses" quickly rot and bubble.

A bright shadow-like figure emerges from it, and enters the King's pumpkin head, loudly cursing at the party. The pumpkin will then grow until it reaches a Huge size, also growing actual carved eyes and mouth, turning into the {@creature The King Of Pumpkins|DVRotPK|King of Pumpkins}. In this shape, he'll disregard any strategy other than using brute strength, and using {@i Pumpkin Visage} to prevent damage.

When he is finally slain, the same spectral figure will emerge, and scream in pain as his voice and silhouette fade away. The amulet will slowly stop glowing, although it will conserve some of its magic. See {@item Shattered Amulet Of Terror|DVRotPK}.

entries.name: Aftermath
entries: When they hear about the mound, the villagers will be absolutely horrified about it, and also extremely thankful of the party's presence. They will insist on throwing a feast in their honor, although pumpkin-related foods will be absent.

entries.name: If Wilburg was rescued,
entries: he'll reward the party with {@b 400 gp} once they are back in Goldgrain, before parting ways.

entries.name: If he wasn't,
entries: it will be Joyce who'll reward the party with {@b 200 gp}.

entries.name: If the party met Farlane,
entries: and Dryleaf has either died or been turned to the town's guard, she'll be willing to perform spells of up to 4th level for them, as long as they acquire the materials. If he was convinced to fight, she'll thank the party for providing fun, but otherwise make no effort to help.

entries.name: If the party let Dryleaf go,
entries: his place will be abandoned, as he had fled the town. Should they decide to loot his place, they'll find lab equipment worth around {@b 600 gp}.

entries.name: If the party convinced Dryleaf to fight the King,
entries: he'll stay at the town, grateful, and will be able to craft potions and poisons for the party (up to Rare). He will charge only the price of the ingredients, and take a quarter of the normal crafting time.
In any of these cases, all the adventurers that helped Goldgrain get rid of the pumpkin-haunting receive {@b 600xp}.
